paper_metadata.title: Improved creep resistance of Mo-V-Si-B alloys with a density below 8 g/cm3

evidence.quote: Ternary Mo-Si-B alloys, consisting of a molybdenum solid solution (Moss) phase and two intermetallic phases Mo5SiB2 (T2) and Mo3Si, are able to combine balanced room temperature fracture toughness, high temperature creep strength and good oxidation performance.
In this study, high potential Mo-V-Si-B materials which provide a reduced density by about 17 % as compared with the reference alloy Mo-9Si-8B were investigated.

The most widely studied alloy Mo-9Si-8B composed of body-centered cubic (bcc) Mo solid solution (Moss), Mo3Si, and Mo5SiB2 obtains a balanced property profile of room- temperature fracture toughness, high-temperature creep strength and oxidation performance [1].

First effects of vanadium alloying on the mechanical properties of Mo-9Si-8B were derived from field assisted sintered (FAST) Mo-40V-9Si-8B alloys, featuring a density reduction by more than 17 % [9].
Initially, investigations were carried out on a Mo-40V-9Si-8B alloy processed via powder metallurgy.

In Addition to that, the creep response of the density-reduced Mo-40V-9Si-8B alloy is evaluated with respect to the three different microstructure types: obtained by processing via (1) field assisted sintering (FAST), (2) FAST and heat treatment (HT) at 1600 ◦C for 10 h and (3) arc melting (Arc).
